evidence.quote: let renewalRefusal (today: DateOnly) (loan: Loan) (library: Library) : LendingError option =
let renewAll (today: DateOnly) memberId (library: Library) : Result<Library * (Loan * Result<Loan, LendingError>) list, LendingError> =
NotRenewable = Loans.renewalRefusal today loan library |> Option.map (renewalReason loan)
| Ok [ "renew"; c ] -> UseCases.renew ports c |> render showRenew

ARC-REV-01.rationale: Tier 2 now holds the whole renewability decision: renewalRefusal checks the reasons in the decision's order, renew uses it, and renewAll is a Tier 2 fold. Tier 3 Views only turns the LendingError returned by Tier 2 into desk wording (renewalReason). It takes the limit from the error and does not re-check any rule. The `loans` listing and `renew` call the same Tier 2 predicate, so they cannot disagree. The CLI used to call Loans.renew directly; the change replaces that with a Tier 3 use case and does not add any new place where the rule is decided.

evidence.quote: let renew ports (copyId: string) : Result<Views.RenewView, LendingError> =

ARC-REV-02.rationale: Tier 1/2 has no new effect: renewalRefusal and renewAll are pure functions of today and the library. The date comes in through the existing Clock port, and persistence goes through the existing commit/Store path. The CLI code it replaces called ports.Store.Load/Save and Loans.renew (Tier 2) straight from presentation. The change removes that and goes through UseCases.renew instead, so it adds no new port bypass and no new direct call from Tier 4 into Tier 2.

ARC-REV-03.rationale: The renewal limit is defined once, in Policy.renewLimit, and both the Tier 2 guard and the Tier 3 view refer to it. They do not copy the value. The refusal reason prints the limit carried in RenewLimitReached. The order of the overdue, limit and holds checks lives only in renewalRefusal, which renew, renewAll and loans all reuse. No literal or predicate is duplicated.

ARC-REV-01.rationale: The new rule (the borrower's member type sets the limit) is decided in Tier 2: Policy.renewLimit maps the member type to the limit, and Loans.renewLimitOf finds the borrower, falling back to Standard. Tier 3 Views calls Loans.renewLimitOf to get the displayed limit instead of working it out itself. The CLI is not changed.

evidence.quote: |> Result.map (fun (l, loan) -> l, Views.ofRenew l loan))

ARC-REV-02.rationale: No effects are added. renewLimitOf and Policy.renewLimit are pure functions over the library. The use cases only pass the library they already have into the view projection. All I/O and the clock still go through the existing ports and commit path.

ARC-REV-03.rationale: The per-type limits (2, 1 and 4) are defined only in Policy.renewLimit. The refusal guard in renewalRefusal and the 'renewal N of M' display both get the limit through the single Tier 2 function renewLimitOf. The 'renewed X of Y times' reason takes it from the RenewLimitReached error, which comes from the same source. The old single-limit constant was replaced, not left alongside, so nothing can drift. The decision document was updated to match.
